fields.statement: Every run the daemon or run start begins picks its workflow through the repo's dispatch rules, keyed by trigger and request kind, with built-in defaults that reproduce plan and ship-change

fields.acceptance: Unit tests in the package that parses the file cover: no file gives plan for every request kind and ship-change for every ready kind; a file setting only [ready] bug changes only that pick; an unknown table, an unknown kind key and a non-string or path-like value each fail with an error naming the table and key
fields.statement: Rhiza reads the repo's committed .rhiza/dispatch.toml: a [request] table (a request is queued) and a [ready] table (a change set is accepted and ready), each mapping a kind (feature, bug, milestone) to a workflow name; a missing file, table or key falls back to the built-in default (request: plan; ready: ship-change), and any other table or key, or a value that is not a bare workflow name, is an error naming it

fields.acceptance: A testscript (dispatch-check) shows rhiza check passing with no dispatch file and with a rule naming a repo workflow in .rhiza/workflows/, and failing with a rule naming a missing workflow and with an unknown table, each failure naming trigger.kind or the table
fields.statement: rhiza check fails on a .rhiza/dispatch.toml that does not parse, or whose rule names a workflow that no layer (personal, repo, built-in) resolves, naming the file, the trigger.kind and the workflow

fields.acceptance: A testscript shows a change set opened by run start --new --request for a bug request with a workflow recording kind bug and that workflow in change show --json, a change set from rhiza change new showing kind feature and no workflow, and the log still folding with fold-ok
fields.statement: A change set records its kind and an optional workflow: the change set a request's plan run opens records that request's kind and the workflow the request named, any other change set (from a milestone plan or rhiza change new) has kind feature and no workflow, and rhiza change show shows both

fields.acceptance: A testscript shows request --workflow naming a repo workflow queued and listed by request ls --json with the workflow, request --workflow naming a missing workflow exiting 2 with the queue unchanged, and describe-golden regenerated for the new request field
fields.statement: rhiza request --workflow <name> stores the name on the queued request, refuses with a usage error (exit 2, nothing queued) a name no layer resolves, and request ls shows it; the request's plan run passes it to the change set it opens, so it overrides only that change set's ready pick

fields.acceptance: Tests in internal/api show a dispatch file mapping [request] bug to a repo workflow making the daemon's start of a bug request run that workflow with --new, a feature request still running plan, and a milestone request mapped to another workflow starting it with --milestone and without --autonomous
fields.statement: The daemon starts a queued request's plan run with the workflow the [request] rule names for the request's kind (default plan), and run start --new accepts that workflow instead of refusing every workflow but plan; a milestone request still opens a record change set and never runs autonomous, whatever workflow its rule names

fields.acceptance: Tests in internal/api show the resolver's order (recorded workflow over rule over ship-change, explicit --workflow over all), and a testscript shows run start --dry-run on a bug change set with [ready] bug set to a repo workflow naming that workflow, and with no dispatch file naming ship-change
fields.statement: One resolver picks the workflow of a ready change set's run, used both by the daemon's ship pick and by rhiza run start <cs> with no --workflow: the change set's recorded workflow, else the [ready] rule for its kind, else ship-change; an explicit run start --workflow always wins

fields.acceptance: Tests in internal/api show a daemon poll with a recorded workflow or a rule naming a workflow that does not resolve starting no run, recording a skip naming the workflow and its source, and listing an inbox item for it, while other candidates in the same poll still start
fields.statement: When the workflow dispatch picks for a request or a ready change set no longer resolves at start time, the daemon starts no run, never falls back to the default, and raises it as attention: a skip reason in daemon status and an inbox item naming the change set or request, the workflow and where the pick came from

fields.acceptance: A testscript shows run start on a change set picked by a [ready] rule recording rule ready.bug, one with no dispatch file recording the default, and one with --workflow recording explicit, each shown by run status --json and run ls --json; a test in internal/api shows the daemon's start log line naming the pick
fields.statement: Each run's journal records which workflow dispatch picked and why (the request's or change set's override, the rule trigger.kind, the built-in default, or an explicit --workflow), rhiza run ls and rhiza run status show it, and the daemon logs it when it starts the run

fields.acceptance: A test of the guide shows the workflows topic naming dispatch.toml, [request], [ready] and request --workflow, and the guide's existing size checks still pass
fields.statement: The workflows guide topic explains .rhiza/dispatch.toml: its two tables, the kinds, the built-in defaults, rhiza request --workflow, the resolution order and how a broken name is reported
